category_title: Students using proactive determination and compensatory work-arounds
minimal_context: The student and tutor are preparing for the matriculation examination by reviewing course materials.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's get started on preparing for the matriculation exam. Please open the textbook to page 45 and read the chapter on the industrial revolution.

STUDENT: I prefer not to read the textbook at all. I brought the summaries my friend wrote and some flow charts we can use instead.

TUTOR: The textbook has the full information you need to know. Go ahead and read the first few paragraphs.

STUDENT: I can prepare for this without opening a book. I usually just speak aloud to myself to memorize the summaries, or you can read the text aloud to me.

TUTOR: Everyone else just reads the textbook directly to study. You need to do the same to get through the material.

STUDENT: I'm not going to say sorry for needing to be read aloud to. It is a thing that I deserve, and I will really insist on my rights to use these accommodations.

options.A: Encourage the student to take the matriculation exams during the preparation process.
options.B: Identify the stage that the student is at in this process using the four coping strategy model.
options.C: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during the study sessions.
options.D: Extend the study sessions to one and a half hours, unlike standard 40-50 minute school lessons.
